UTA.head: This one sets up well for the Mammoth
UTA.body: Even though Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. On top of that, Vancouver is on the second night of a back-to-back. It’s on the Canucks to make it a game, and they can if their power play gets going.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Canucks?
paras: The Mammoth are winless in five (0-2-3), while the Canucks (4-17-1) beat Vegas 6-3 last night. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Mammoth fifth in the Central (tied for 15th in the NHL).

The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.205) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .339, and their goaltending has held them back. The Mammoth have played better than their record (.548) says: their chances are worth about .692, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Canucks (32nd) and the Mammoth (30th) both have had shaky goaltending. The Canucks have a leaky penalty kill (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). Vancouver has allowed 4.45 goals a game, the most in the league. On the other side, the Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st). The Mammoth are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Canucks. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Elias Pettersson (#40) (6 G / 17 A / 23 P in 22 GP) leads the Canucks in scoring, and Brock Boeser (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 22 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Mammoth, Clayton Keller (5 G / 22 A / 27 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in six straight games against Vancouver. Mikhail Sergachev (6 G / 16 A / 22 P in 21 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Nikita Tolopilo is expected to go for Vancouver, his first start of the season. Karel Vejmelka (6-6-2 / .869 SV% in 14 GS) has struggled for Utah so far, but is expected to start.
The Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Canucks do.

items.text: The Mammoth are newly without Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther, and have been without Nate Schmidt and John Marino for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche are missing more right now.
Brendan Gallagher has no goals on chances worth about 3.3 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Brock Boeser has a point in seven straight games.
Vincent Trocheck is one assist from 400.
